hero.headline: THE WALL CRACKED. SPAIN DIDN'T.
hero.standfirst: Belgium did what nobody had managed in six games — they scored past Spain. It bought them 47 minutes of hope. Then Mikel Merino came off the bench and, for the second time in six days, won a World Cup knockout tie — 117 seconds after stepping on the pitch. France–Spain, the final everyone wanted, arrives a round early on Tuesday.

facts.text: De Ketelaere's equaliser was the first goal Spain conceded in the entire tournament — Unai Simón's record run ended at last
Merino scored 117 seconds after coming on — his second knockout winner from the bench in six days
Belgium lost captain Tielemans in the warm-up and Courtois to injury during the game

yesterday.report: The night began badly for Belgium before it began at all: captain Youri Tielemans pulled up injured in the warm-up. Yet they matched Spain punch for punch — Fabián Ruiz hammered in a 30th-minute rebound after Courtois spilled Olmo's shot, and four minutes before the break Charles De Ketelaere did what nobody in six games had done: he beat Unai Simón, ending Spain's perfect defensive record.
yesterday.report2: With Courtois himself forced off injured, the tie hung level until the 88th minute — when the script repeated itself. Substitute Mikel Merino, on for less than two minutes, turned home the rebound after backup keeper Lammens spilled Cubarsí's shot. Two knockout winners in six days, both from the bench. Spain march on to a Tuesday semi-final against France that feels like a final arriving early.

star.name: Mikel Merino
star.line: The 91st minute against Portugal, the 88th against Belgium, 117 seconds after coming on. Whatever Spain pay their bench, it isn't enough.

aside.name: Charles De Ketelaere
aside.line: The man who finally scored past Spain — the only one in six games. A piece of history as consolation for a heartbreaking exit.

yesterday.whatItMeans: France–Spain in Tuesday's Dallas semi-final: the two form sides of the tournament, one step from MetLife. Belgium exit with heads high and a hospital ward of bad luck.

today.kicker: QF3 · THE BEST NO. 9 v THE DEEPEST SQUAD
today.preview: Norway's first quarter-final in history against an England side that survived the Azteca with ten men. Haaland — born in Leeds while his father played there — has 7 goals and buried Brazil almost single-handed; England counter with Bellingham's form, Kane's ice and genuine depth. One complication: Quansah's suspension carves a hole in England's back line precisely where Haaland does his work.
watch: Haaland can join Messi and Mbappé on 8 — or pass them
Bellingham against the tournament's biggest stage, again
The winner faces Argentina or Switzerland in Wednesday's Atlanta semi

keyMan.name: Erling Haaland
keyMan.line: Seven goals, a nation's first quarter-final, and the country of his birth in the way. Norway don't need much possession — they need him twice.

factors.label: FORM
factors.text: Norway have won the knockout ties that mattered, with Haaland scoring 7 of the team's goals. England survived a ten-man siege at the Azteca — battered, but battle-tested.

factors.label: THE MATCH-UP
factors.text: Haaland was born in Leeds while his father Alfie played in the Premier League. The striker England's football raised now stands between them and the semi-final.

factors.label: FITNESS & FATIGUE
factors.text: England are without Jarell Quansah, suspended since the Azteca red card — a gap at centre-back exactly where Haaland operates. Both squads have had a full week's rest.

factors.label: WHERE THE MONEY IS
factors.text: The biggest market of the tournament: $2.4m traded on Kalshi, pricing England 52%, the draw 27%, Norway 24% in regulation. Respect for Haaland is baked into that 24.

prediction.verdict: England have more ways to win, and the market agrees. But Norway only need the game to be close for Haaland to decide it, and the man marking him is a stand-in. England — with less confidence than the number suggests, and a real chance the family is watching extra time at 1 AM.
